title_en: Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (for Trial Implementation)
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (For Trial Implementation)

(Adopted at the 499th Session of the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court on May 29, 1991)
Fa (Xing) Fa [1991] No. 19

I. Scope of Accepting Cases

1. "Specific administrative act" refers to a unilateral act taken by a state administrative organ or its staff members, an organization authorized by laws or regulations, an organization or individual entrusted by an administrative organ, in the course of administrative management activities, exercising administrative authority, directed at specific citizens, legal persons or other organizations, with respect to specific concrete matters, and concerning the rights and obligations of such citizens, legal persons or other organizations.

2. In accordance with the scope of accepting cases provided in Article 11 of the Administrative Procedure Law, a citizen who is dissatisfied with a decision on re-education through labor made by the Labor Re-education Management Committee may file an administrative lawsuit with the People's Court.

A citizen who is dissatisfied with a decision on compulsory custody for examination made by a public security organ may file an administrative lawsuit with the People's Court.

A citizen who is dissatisfied with an administrative penalty of collecting a fee for exceeding the birth quota or a fine imposed by the competent family planning authority may file an administrative lawsuit with the People's Court.

3. The term "law" in Article 12(4) of the Administrative Procedure Law, which provides that "specific administrative acts for which the law provides that the administrative organ shall make a final decision," refers to normative documents formulated, adopted and promulgated by the National People's Congress and its Standing Committee in accordance with the legislative procedure.

Where regulations or rules provide that an administrative organ may make a "final decision" on certain matters, and a citizen, legal person or other organization, dissatisfied with the "final decision" made by the administrative organ pursuant to such regulations or rules, files a lawsuit with the People's Court in accordance with the law, the People's Court shall accept the case.

4. A citizen, legal person or other organization who is dissatisfied with a decision made by an administrative organ on a compensation matter may file an administrative lawsuit with the People's Court.

5. A citizen, legal person or other organization who is dissatisfied with a compulsory compensation decision made by an administrative organ in accordance with its authority may file an administrative lawsuit in accordance with the law.

6. Where an administrative organ mediates civil rights disputes between citizens, legal persons or other organizations, or makes an arbitration award in accordance with the provisions of laws or regulations, and a party dissatisfied with the mediation or arbitration files a lawsuit with the People's Court, the People's Court shall not accept the case as an administrative case.

7. Where a citizen, legal person or other organization is dissatisfied with a decision made by a People's Government or its competent department concerning the ownership or right to use of resources such as land, minerals, or forests, and files a lawsuit with the People's Court in accordance with the law, the People's Court shall accept the case as an administrative case.

8. Where a citizen, legal person or other organization files an administrative lawsuit with the People's Court against a non-official act of an administrative organ's staff member, the People's Court shall not accept the case.

II. Jurisdiction

9. Specialized People's Courts shall not set up administrative divisions and shall not accept administrative cases.

10. Any of the following three circumstances constitutes a "reconsideration organ changing the original specific administrative act" as provided in Article 17 of the Administrative Procedure Law:

(1) The reconsideration organ changes the facts found in the original specific administrative act;
(2) The reconsideration organ changes the laws, regulations or rules applied in the original specific administrative act;
(3) The reconsideration organ changes the result of the original specific administrative act, i.e., revokes it in whole or in part, or modifies it.

11. The term "the place where the plaintiff is located" in Article 18 of the Administrative Procedure Law includes the plaintiff's domicile, habitual residence, and the place where the plaintiff's personal freedom is restricted.

III. Participants in Proceedings

12. Where a citizen entitled to file a lawsuit dies, the near relative who files the lawsuit shall be the plaintiff. Near relatives include spouses, parents, children, siblings, grandparents, maternal grandparents, grandchildren, and maternal grandchildren.

13. Where two or more parties are dissatisfied with the same specific administrative act and file lawsuits with the People's Court, they are joint plaintiffs.

14. Where another organization without the status of a legal person files an administrative lawsuit with the People's Court, the principal responsible person of that organization shall act as its legal representative; if there is no principal responsible person, the de facto responsible person may act as the legal representative.

15. During the proceedings, if the principal responsible person of a legal person or other organization acting as the plaintiff, or of an administrative organ acting as the defendant, is replaced, resulting in a change of the legal representative participating in the proceedings, a certificate of identity of the new legal representative shall be submitted to the People's Court, and the new legal representative shall continue to participate in the proceedings; the litigation activities already conducted shall be binding on the legal representative who continues to participate.

16. Where the reconsideration organ fails to make a reconsideration decision within the statutory period, and a party dissatisfied with the original specific administrative act files a lawsuit with the People's Court, the administrative organ that made the original specific administrative act shall be the defendant.

17. During the first-instance proceedings, the People's Court may, with the consent of the plaintiff, add or change the defendant ex officio. Where the defendant should be changed but the plaintiff does not agree, the People's Court shall rule to dismiss the lawsuit.

18. Where a citizen, legal person or other organization, dissatisfied with a specific administrative act made by a dispatched agency of an administrative organ, files a lawsuit with the People's Court, the administrative organ shall be the defendant; except where laws or regulations grant authority to the dispatched agency.

19. Where a citizen, legal person or other organization, dissatisfied with a decision made jointly by an administrative organ and a non-administrative organ under their joint signature, files an administrative lawsuit with the People's Court, the administrative organ that made the decision shall be the defendant, and the non-administrative organ cannot be the defendant. However, if compensation is needed for infringing upon the lawful rights and interests of a citizen, legal person or other organization, the People's Court may notify the non-administrative organ to participate in the proceedings as a third party.

20. When the People's Court summons a party to appear in court, a summons shall always be used.

21. The phrase "having an interest in the specific administrative act being sued" in Article 27 of the Administrative Procedure Law refers to having a legal relationship of rights and obligations with the specific administrative act being sued.

22. Where an administrative organ imposes penalties on two or more joint violators for the same illegal fact, and some of the penalty recipients, dissatisfied with the penalty decision, file a lawsuit with the People's Court, if the People's Court finds that other punished persons who have not filed a lawsuit have a legal interest in the specific administrative act being sued, it shall notify them to participate in the proceedings as third parties.

23. A third party has the right to file claims related to the case; if dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment of the People's Court, it has the right to file an appeal.

24. When a party appoints a litigation representative, a power of attorney shall be submitted to the People's Court. The power of attorney shall specify the matters entrusted and the scope of authority, and shall be examined and approved by the People's Court. The termination of the appointment shall be reported in writing to the People's Court.

25. When a social organization accepts an appointment, the legal representative of that social organization shall be the appointed litigation representative. With the consent of the principal, the legal representative of the social organization may designate a member of that social organization or retain a lawyer as the litigation representative.

26. Parties and their litigation representatives may make excerpts of trial materials permitted for inspection, but may not make copies without authorization.

27. Where the reconsideration organ changes the original specific administrative act, the reconsideration organ is the defendant; however, the reconsideration organ may entrust one or two staff members of the original decision-making organ as litigation representatives, or may entrust its own staff members or a lawyer as litigation representatives in accordance with the law.

IV. Evidence

28. In accordance with the provisions of Article 33 of the Administrative Procedure Law, during the proceedings, the defendant shall not collect evidence from the plaintiff or witnesses on its own; lawyers acting as litigation representatives of the defendant shall likewise not collect evidence from the plaintiff or witnesses on their own.

29. Where there is a dispute as to whether the plaintiff's lawsuit has exceeded the time limit for prosecution, the defendant bears the burden of proof.

30. Where the defendant fails to provide, or is unable to provide, the main evidence and the normative documents on which the specific administrative act is based before the conclusion of the first-instance trial, the People's Court may, in accordance with the provisions of Article 32 and Article 54(2) of the Administrative Procedure Law, rule to revoke the specific administrative act being sued.

V. Prosecution and Acceptance

31. Where the law provides that a party dissatisfied with a specific administrative act of an administrative organ may either file a lawsuit with the People's Court or apply for reconsideration with the reconsideration organ making a final decision, if the party has chosen to apply for reconsideration, the party may no longer file an administrative lawsuit with the People's Court. If the party both files a lawsuit and applies for reconsideration, the organ that first receives the relevant materials shall be deemed the organ chosen by the party; if the materials are received simultaneously, the party shall make the choice.

32. Where a party dissatisfied with a specific administrative act of an administrative organ should, in accordance with the law, first apply for reconsideration, and the party files a lawsuit directly with the People's Court without applying for reconsideration, the People's Court shall not accept the case.

33. Where no law or regulation provides that a party dissatisfied with a specific administrative act of an administrative organ may file a lawsuit with the People's Court, and the party files a lawsuit with the People's Court against a specific administrative act made by the administrative organ before the implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law, the People's Court shall not accept the case. However, if the party only learns of the specific administrative act after the implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law, the People's Court shall accept the case in accordance with the law.

34. Where an administrative organ, when making a specific administrative act, does not prepare or serve a decision document, and a party, dissatisfied with the specific administrative act, files a lawsuit with the People's Court, as long as the party can prove the existence of the specific administrative act and meets other conditions for prosecution, the People's Court shall accept the case.

35. Where an administrative organ, when making a specific administrative act, fails to inform the party of the right to sue or the time limit for prosecution, causing the party to file a lawsuit beyond the time limit, the time limit for prosecution shall be calculated from the date when the party actually learns of the right to sue or the time limit for prosecution; however, the overdue period shall not exceed one year at most.

36. Where a party is still dissatisfied with a specific administrative act re-made by the administrative organ after the People's Court's judgment has revoked the original specific administrative act, the party may file a lawsuit with the People's Court as a new administrative case. If the administrative organ, based on the same facts and reasons, re-makes a specific administrative act substantially identical to the original one, the People's Court shall, in accordance with Article 54(2) and Article 55 of the Administrative Procedure Law, rule to revoke it, and handle the matter in accordance with the provisions of Article 65(3).

37. In a public security administrative case, if the reconsideration organ revokes the original penalty decision, and the victim, dissatisfied, files a lawsuit in accordance with the law, the People's Court shall accept the case.

38. Where a victim or a person penalized is dissatisfied with a warning or a fine of not more than 50 yuan imposed by a police substation in accordance with Article 33(2) of the Regulations on Administrative Penalties for Public Security, and applies for reconsideration to the public security organ that established the police substation, and the reconsideration organ changes the original decision by imposing a fine of over 50 yuan or a detention penalty, and the party is dissatisfied with the reconsideration decision, the party may file a lawsuit directly with the People's Court.

39. Where a victim believes that the person penalized has committed two acts violating public security administration in the same incident, but the public security organ only recognizes and penalizes one of them, and the victim files a lawsuit demanding that the public security organ penalize the other act, the People's Court shall not accept the case.

40. Upon receiving the plaintiff's complaint, the People's Court shall have the administrative division review it. If the conditions for prosecution are met, it shall docket the case within seven days; if the conditions are not met, it shall render a ruling of non-acceptance within seven days.

41. Where a law or regulation only provides that a party dissatisfied with a specific type of specific administrative act may apply for reconsideration, but does not provide for filing a lawsuit with the People's Court, and the Administrative Procedure Law provides that a lawsuit may be filed with the People's Court, when the party files a lawsuit with the People's Court, the court shall inform the party to apply for reconsideration with the administrative organ.

42. Where an administrative organ, in a single specific administrative act, makes different treatments according to different laws or regulations, the time limits for prosecution shall be calculated separately in accordance with the provisions of the corresponding laws or regulations. The People's Court shall accept the part of the lawsuit that has not exceeded the time limit for prosecution; the part that has exceeded the time limit shall not be accepted.

43. Where an administrative organ, based on two or more laws or regulations, makes a single specific administrative act with only one item of treatment, and the time limits for prosecution provided by the laws or regulations are inconsistent, when the party files a lawsuit, as long as it does not exceed the longest time limit for prosecution, the People's Court shall accept the case.

44. Where an administrative organ, based on the same facts, makes specific administrative acts against several persons, and according to the law, a party dissatisfied with such specific administrative acts may either apply for reconsideration to the higher-level administrative organ with the reconsideration organ making a final decision, or file a lawsuit directly with the People's Court, if some persons choose to apply for reconsideration, these persons may no longer file a lawsuit with the People's Court, while the other persons may still file a lawsuit with the People's Court in accordance with the law.

45. Where a law or regulation provides that a party dissatisfied with a specific administrative act must undergo reconsideration before filing a lawsuit with the People's Court, and if the administrative organ adds a party in the reconsideration decision, the added party, if dissatisfied with the reconsideration decision, may file a lawsuit directly with the People's Court.

VI. Trial and Judgment

46. Where a single act of a party simultaneously violates two or more laws or regulations, and if different competent administrative organs impose administrative penalties based on the different laws or regulations, and all penalized parties, dissatisfied, file lawsuits with the People's Court, the People's Court may consolidate the cases for trial.

47. Where an administrative organ, based on the same facts, makes separate administrative decisions against several persons, and the penalized persons, dissatisfied, file separate lawsuits with the People's Court, the People's Court may, depending on the circumstances, decide to consolidate the cases for trial or try them separately.

48. During the proceedings, if the defendant discovers that the plaintiff has committed a new illegal act and imposes a penalty for it, and if the plaintiff, dissatisfied with the new penalty decision, files a lawsuit with the People's Court, the People's Court may try the case separately or consolidate it with the original case.

49. A party's application for withdrawal shall be made at the commencement of the trial; if the grounds for withdrawal become known after the commencement of the trial, the application may also be made before the conclusion of the court debate. The application for withdrawal may be made orally or in writing.

The person subject to the application for withdrawal shall suspend participation in the work of this case until the People's Court makes a decision on whether to grant the withdrawal; except where urgent measures need to be taken in the case.

50. The People's Court shall make a decision on the party's application for withdrawal orally or in writing within three days of the application. If the applicant is dissatisfied with the decision, the applicant may apply for reconsideration once at the time of receiving the decision. During the reconsideration period, the person subject to the application for withdrawal shall not suspend participation in the work of this case. The People's Court shall make a reconsideration decision on the reconsideration application within three days and notify the reconsideration applicant.

51. For cases where it may become impossible or difficult to enforce the judgment due to the conduct of one party or for other reasons, the People's Court may, upon application of the other party, make a ruling on property preservation; even if no party has made the application, the People's Court may, when necessary, rule to adopt property preservation measures.

When adopting property preservation measures, the People's Court may order the applicant to provide security; if the applicant fails to provide security, the application shall be dismissed.

After accepting the application, if the situation is urgent, the People's Court must make a ruling within 48 hours; if it rules to adopt property preservation measures, execution shall commence immediately.

52. Property preservation shall be limited to the scope of the claims involved in the litigation, or to property related to this case.

Property preservation measures include sealing up, distraining, freezing, or other methods provided by law.

53. If the person against whom property preservation is applied provides security, the People's Court shall lift the property preservation.

54. If the application for property preservation is erroneous, the applicant shall compensate the person against whom it is applied for the losses suffered as a result of the property preservation.

55. For cases in which an administrative organ is accused of failing to pay pensions in accordance with the law, the People's Court may, upon the party's application, issue a written ruling for advance execution.

56. If a party is dissatisfied with a ruling on property preservation or advance execution, the party may apply for reconsideration once. The execution of the ruling shall not be suspended during the reconsideration period.

57. During the proceedings, if an administrative organ applies to the People's Court for compulsory enforcement of the specific administrative act being sued, the People's Court shall not enforce it. When necessary, the People's Court may adopt property preservation measures.

58. If the administrative organ being sued is not located in the same region as the People's Court hearing the case, and the People's Court applies local regulations when trying the administrative case, it shall base its decision on the local regulations legally applied by the administrative organ that made the specific administrative act.

59. If the plaintiff, without justifiable reasons, fails to appear in court after being legally summoned twice, it shall be deemed as withdrawal of the lawsuit, and the People's Court may, depending on the circumstances, rule to permit or not permit the withdrawal.

60. If the People's Court rules not to permit the plaintiff to withdraw the lawsuit, and the plaintiff still fails to appear in court, the People's Court may make a default judgment by analogy with the provisions of Article 48 of the Administrative Procedure Law.

61. If the People's Court rules to permit the plaintiff to withdraw the lawsuit, and the plaintiff files another lawsuit, the People's Court shall not accept it.

If the plaintiff fails to prepay the litigation fee within the statutory period and does not apply for a deferment of the litigation fee, and the case is treated as withdrawn by the plaintiff, and the plaintiff files another lawsuit within the period for prosecution, the People's Court shall accept it.

62. If the defendant administrative organ changes the specific administrative act it made during the first-instance proceedings, and if the plaintiff's application for withdrawal has not been granted, or if the plaintiff does not apply for withdrawal, the People's Court shall continue to try the original specific administrative act being sued.

63. During the trial of an administrative case, if the People's Court finds that the conduct of the penalized party constitutes a crime and criminal liability should be pursued, if the pursuit of criminal liability does not affect the trial of this case, the trial shall continue, and the relevant criminal materials shall be promptly transferred to the relevant authority; if the pursuit of criminal liability affects the trial of this case, the proceedings shall be suspended, the relevant criminal materials shall be transferred to the relevant authority for handling, and after the relevant authority has made a final decision, the proceedings shall be resumed.

64. During the proceedings, the proceedings shall be suspended under any of the following circumstances:

(1) The plaintiff dies, and it is necessary to await the near relative's indication of whether to participate in the proceedings;
(2) The plaintiff loses the capacity for litigation, and no legal representative has been determined;
(3) The legal person or other organization acting as the plaintiff is terminated, and no person succeeding to its rights and obligations has been determined;
(4) A party is unable to participate in the proceedings due to force majeure;
(5) Other circumstances where proceedings should be suspended.

After the reasons for suspension are eliminated, the proceedings shall be resumed.

If, due to the reasons in subparagraphs (1), (2) or (3) of the first paragraph of this Article, the proceedings have been suspended for three full months and still no one continues the proceedings, the proceedings shall be terminated.

65. If the People's Court rules to revoke the original specific administrative act that was upheld by the reconsideration organ, the reconsideration decision shall naturally become invalid.

66. When trying an administrative case, the People's Court may not directly impose an administrative penalty on a person who should have been subject to an administrative penalty by an administrative organ but was not.

67. If, when the People's Court rules that the defendant shall re-make a specific administrative act, the defendant re-makes the specific administrative act, as long as part of the facts or reasons are changed, it shall not be considered the "same facts and reasons" as provided in Article 55 of the Administrative Procedure Law.

68. If the People's Court rules to revoke a specific administrative act of an administrative organ on the ground of violation of legal procedures, when the administrative organ re-makes the specific administrative act, it is not subject to the restriction of Article 55 of the Administrative Procedure Law.

69. The names of the legal documents in administrative cases tried by the People's Courts are administrative judgments, administrative rulings, administrative compensation mediation agreements, and so forth.

70. When a People's Court needs to refer to rules or regulations in rendering a judgment or ruling, it shall state: "In accordance with Article 53 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and with reference to the provisions of [name of rules/regulations (article, paragraph, item)]."

71. Rulings are applicable to the following scope:
(1) rejecting the initiation of a lawsuit;
(2) dismissing the lawsuit;
(3) suspending the execution of a specific administrative act during the litigation period or rejecting an application for suspension of execution;
(4) property preservation and advance execution;
(5) permitting or not permitting withdrawal of the lawsuit;
(6) suspending or terminating the litigation;
(7) correcting clerical errors in a judgment;
(8) suspending or terminating execution;
(9) other matters that require a ruling.
With respect to rulings under items (1) and (2), a party may appeal.
A ruling shall be signed by the members of the collegial panel and the court clerk, and shall bear the seal of the People's Court. If an oral ruling is made in accordance with the law, it shall be recorded in the transcript.

72. After a first-instance judgment, if one or some of the parties appeal, and the appeal concerns a severable claim, the parties who did not appeal may not be listed in the legal document; if the appeal still concerns an inseparable claim, the parties who did not appeal may be listed as appellees.

73. If an appeal petition is submitted through the court of first instance, copies equal to the number of opposing parties shall be submitted.
If a party appeals directly to the court of second instance, the court of second instance shall, within five days, transmit the appeal petition to the court of first instance.
Upon receipt of the appeal petition, the court of first instance or the court of second instance shall immediately notify the opposing party.

74. Upon receipt of the appeal petition, the court of first instance shall, within five days, serve a copy of the appeal petition on the opposing party. The opposing party, upon receipt of the copy of the appeal petition, shall submit a reply within ten days. The failure of a party to submit a reply shall not affect the trial by the People's Court.
Upon receipt of the appeal petition and the reply, the court of first instance shall, together with the complete case file and evidence, promptly submit them to the court of second instance.

75. When hearing an appealed case, the court of second instance must comprehensively review whether the facts ascertained by the court of first instance are clear, whether the application of laws and regulations is correct, and whether there were any violations of legal procedures, without being limited by the scope of the appeal.

76. In the proceedings of second instance, the administrative organ may not alter its original specific administrative act. If the appellant applies to withdraw the appeal because the administrative organ has altered its original specific administrative act, the People's Court shall not permit it.

77. When hearing an appeal against a first-instance ruling rejecting the initiation of a lawsuit, if the court of second instance finds that the case should be accepted, it shall render a ruling to revoke the first-instance ruling and instruct the original court of first instance to docket and accept the case.
When hearing an appeal against a first-instance ruling dismissing the lawsuit, if the court of second instance finds that the first-instance ruling was erroneous, it shall render a ruling to revoke the first-instance ruling and remand the case to the original court of first instance for a new trial.

78. For an administrative case that the court of second instance remands by ruling to the court of first instance for a new trial, the original court of first instance shall form a new collegial panel to conduct the trial.

79. When hearing an appealed case, if the court of second instance needs to amend the judgment, it shall revoke or partially revoke the first-instance judgment and, in accordance with the law, render a judgment to affirm, revoke, or modify the specific administrative act under challenge.

80. For a case decided to be retried through trial supervision procedures, a ruling shall be made to suspend the execution of the original judgment. The ruling shall be signed by the president of the court and bear the seal of the People's Court.

VII. Execution

81. Administrative judgments, rulings, and administrative compensation mediation agreements that have taken legal effect shall be executed by the court of first instance.

82. Where an administrative organ applies to the People's Court for compulsory execution of its specific administrative act in accordance with Article 66 of the Administrative Procedure Law, the basic people's court at the location of the person subject to execution shall accept and handle the execution. If a basic people's court finds that execution by an intermediate people's court is necessary, it may report to the intermediate people's court for a decision.

83. Where the law provides that a specific administrative act is subject to final adjudication by an administrative organ, and the administrative organ applies to the People's Court for compulsory execution, the People's Court shall not execute it.

84. Where a citizen, legal person, or other organization neither files a lawsuit within the statutory time limit, nor performs the specific administrative act, and the law or regulation provides that the administrative organ shall enforce it compulsorily in accordance with the law, if the administrative organ applies to the People's Court for compulsory execution, the People's Court shall not execute it.
Where a citizen, legal person, or other organization neither files a lawsuit within the statutory time limit, nor performs the specific administrative act, and the law or regulation provides that the administrative organ may enforce it compulsorily in accordance with the law or may also apply to the People's Court for compulsory execution, if the administrative organ applies to the People's Court for compulsory execution, the People's Court shall execute it.
Where a citizen, legal person, or other organization neither files a lawsuit within the statutory time limit, nor performs the specific administrative act, and the administrative organ has no statutory power of compulsory execution and applies to the People's Court for compulsory execution, the People's Court shall execute it.

85. Where an administrative organ applies to the People's Court for compulsory execution in accordance with the law, it shall submit an application for execution, the legal document serving as the basis for execution, and other necessary materials. If the person subject to execution is a citizen, the person subject to execution or his adult family member shall be notified to be present; if the person subject to execution is a legal person or other organization, its legal representative or principal responsible person shall be notified to be present. Refusal to be present shall not affect the execution. If the person subject to execution is a citizen, the unit where he works or the grassroots organization at the location of the property shall send personnel to participate.

86. With respect to an administrative judgment, ruling, or administrative compensation mediation agreement of the People's Court that has taken legal effect, if one party refuses to perform, the other party may, in accordance with Article 65 of the Administrative Procedure Law, apply to the People's Court for compulsory execution.
Upon receipt of the application for execution or the referral for execution, the executing officer shall, within ten days, review the facts of the case and notify the person subject to execution to perform within a specified period. If the person fails to perform within the specified period, compulsory execution shall be carried out.

87. The time limit for a party to apply to the court of first instance for execution of an effective judgment or ruling is three months. The time limit for applying for execution shall be calculated from the last day of the period specified in the legal document. If no period for performance is specified in the legal document, it shall be calculated from the date the legal document takes effect. Applications submitted after the time limit shall not be executed unless there is a justifiable reason.

88. With respect to applications by administrative organs to the People's Court for compulsory execution of their specific administrative acts, the execution division shall be responsible for review and execution. The time limit for applying for execution is three months from the date the period for filing a lawsuit expires. Applications submitted after the time limit shall not be accepted by the People's Court.
The funds or property executed shall be delivered to the administrative organ that applied for execution. The People's Court shall collect execution fees in accordance with the law.

89. When the People's Court takes compulsory execution measures against a citizen, legal person, or other organization, it may rule to freeze or transfer the deposits of the person subject to execution, or to withhold or attach the labor income of the person subject to execution; it may also rule to seal up, seize, freeze, auction, or sell off the property of the person subject to execution.
When taking the above measures, the People's Court shall not exceed the scope of the obligations that the person subject to execution should perform; if the person subject to execution is a citizen, the necessary living expenses and necessities for the person subject to execution and the family members he supports shall be retained.

90. When the People's Court rules to freeze or transfer deposits or to withhold or attach income, it shall issue a notice of assistance in execution. The unit where the person subject to execution works, banks, credit cooperatives, and other entities with savings business must handle the matter.

91. When the People's Court seals up or seizes property, if the person subject to execution is a citizen, the person subject to execution or his adult family member shall be notified to be present; if the person subject to execution is a legal person or other organization, its legal representative or principal responsible person shall be notified to be present. Refusal to be present shall not affect the execution. If the person subject to execution is a citizen, the unit where he works or the grassroots organization at the location of the property shall send personnel to participate.

92. With respect to sealed-up or seized property, the executing officer must prepare an inventory, which shall be signed or sealed by the persons present, and a copy shall be given to the person subject to execution. If the person subject to execution is a citizen, a copy may also be given to his adult family member.

93. After property is sealed up or seized, the executing officer shall order the person subject to execution to fulfill the obligations determined by the legal document within a specified period. If the person subject to execution fails to fulfill them within the specified period, the People's Court may, in accordance with regulations, deliver the sealed-up or seized property to the relevant entity for auction or sale. Items prohibited from free trading by the State shall be delivered to the relevant entity for purchase at the price stipulated by the State.

94. For compulsory eviction from a house, compulsory demolition of an illegal structure, or compulsory vacation of land, the president of the court shall issue a public notice ordering the person subject to execution to perform within a specified period. If the person subject to execution fails to perform within the specified period, the executing officer shall carry out compulsory execution.
During compulsory execution, if the person subject to execution is a citizen, the person subject to execution or his adult family member shall be notified to be present; if the person subject to execution is a legal person or other organization, its legal representative or principal responsible person shall be notified to be present. Refusal to be present shall not affect the execution. If the person subject to execution is a citizen, the unit where he works or the grassroots organization at the location of the house or land shall send personnel to participate. The executing officer shall record the circumstances of the compulsory execution in a transcript, which shall be signed or sealed by the persons present.
Property removed during compulsory eviction from a house shall be transported by personnel from the People's Court to a designated location and delivered to the person subject to execution. If the person subject to execution is a citizen, it may also be delivered to his adult family member. Losses caused by refusal to accept delivery shall be borne by the person subject to execution.

95. Under any of the following circumstances, the People's Court shall rule to suspend execution:
(1) the applicant indicates that execution may be deferred;
(2) a person not involved in the case raises a well-founded objection to the subject matter of execution;
(3) a citizen who is a party dies and the court is awaiting the succession of rights or assumption of obligations by an heir;
(4) a legal person or other organization that is a party is dissolved and the successor of rights or obligations has not yet been determined;
(5) other circumstances under which the People's Court considers execution should be suspended.
After the circumstances causing suspension cease, execution shall resume.

96. Under any of the following circumstances, the People's Court shall rule to terminate execution:
(1) the applicant withdraws the application;
(2) the legal document serving as the basis for execution is revoked;
(3) the citizen subject to execution dies, leaving no estate available for execution and no one to assume the obligations;
(4) the person entitled to a pension in a case for recovery of pension dies;
(5) other circumstances under which the People's Court considers execution should be terminated.

97. The ruling of the People's Court to suspend or terminate execution shall take effect immediately upon service on the parties.

VIII. Liability for Tort Compensation

98. A citizen, legal person, or other organization may file an administrative compensation lawsuit together with the administrative lawsuit at the time of initiating the administrative litigation, or may file the administrative compensation lawsuit during the course of the administrative litigation.

99. If a citizen, legal person, or other organization is dissatisfied with the administrative compensation decision made by an administrative organ, they may file a lawsuit with the People's Court within thirty days from the date of receiving the written administrative compensation decision, unless otherwise provided by laws or regulations.

100. Mediation may be applied in an administrative compensation lawsuit, or the court may directly render a judgment to affirm or modify the administrative compensation decision.

IX. Time Periods

101. Time periods in administrative litigation shall be calculated from the day after the start date. When a time period is not calculated from the first day of a month, one month shall be thirty days.

102. If the last day of a time period falls on a Sunday or other legal holiday, the time period may be extended accordingly. Time in transit shall not be included in the time period.

103. If a basic people's court applies for an extension of the case handling period, it shall directly report to the high people's court for approval, and simultaneously report to the intermediate people's court for the record.

X. Litigation Costs

104. Where there are two or more plaintiffs in the same case, the plaintiff who first initiates the lawsuit shall prepay the litigation costs; if the lawsuits are initiated simultaneously, the prepayment of litigation costs shall be resolved through consultation among the plaintiffs; if consultation fails, the People's Court shall decide.

105. If the judgment of the court of second instance simultaneously revokes the first-instance judgment and the specific administrative act under challenge, the litigation costs of both the first and second instances shall be borne by the administrative organ that was challenged.

106. If the People's Court renders a judgment partially affirming and partially revoking the specific administrative act of the administrative organ, the litigation costs shall be borne by the plaintiff and the defendant in proportion to their respective liability.

107. During the litigation process, if the defendant alters its specific administrative act and the plaintiff applies to withdraw the lawsuit, and the People's Court grants the withdrawal by ruling, the case acceptance fee shall be borne by the defendant and collected at half the rate; other litigation costs shall be collected according to actual expenses. If the plaintiff does not withdraw the lawsuit or the People's Court does not permit the withdrawal, the litigation costs shall be borne by the losing party.

108. If the plaintiff or appellant fails to prepay the litigation costs within the statutory time limit and does not apply for a deferral, the case shall be treated as automatically withdrawn.

109. In an administrative lawsuit, if the specific administrative act under challenge involves a disputed price or amount, the parties shall prepay the litigation costs according to the fee schedule for property cases.

110. No litigation costs shall be collected for cases where the People's Court rules to reject the initiation of a lawsuit.

XI. Foreign-Related Administrative Litigation

111. For a foreign national, stateless person, or foreign enterprise or organization without a domicile within the territory of the People's Republic of China who entrusts a lawyer or other person of the People's Republic of China to act as agent ad litem, the power of attorney sent or entrusted from outside the territory of the People's Republic of China shall be notarized by a notary office in the country where the principal is located, and certified by the embassy or consulate of the People's Republic of China in that country, or shall undergo the certification procedures specified in the relevant treaties concluded between the People's Republic of China and that country, before it becomes effective.

112. The People's Court may serve litigation documents on a party without a domicile within the territory of the People's Republic of China by the following methods:
(1) service in accordance with the methods provided in international treaties concluded or jointly acceded to by the country where the recipient is located and the People's Republic of China;
(2) service through diplomatic channels;
(3) for a recipient of Chinese nationality, service may be entrusted to the embassy or consulate of the People's Republic of China in the country where the recipient is located;
(4) service on the agent ad litem authorized by the recipient to accept service;
(5) service on the representative office established within the territory of the People's Republic of China by the recipient, or on the branch or business agent authorized to accept service;
(6) if the law of the country where the recipient is located permits service by mail, service may be made by mail. If six months have elapsed since the date of mailing and the receipt of service has not been returned, but based on all circumstances it is sufficient to confirm that service has been made, the date of expiry of the period shall be deemed the date of service;
(7) if service cannot be made by any of the above methods, service shall be made by public notice. After six months have elapsed from the date of public notice, service shall be deemed to have been made.

113. A party without a domicile within the territory of the People's Republic of China who is dissatisfied with the judgment or ruling of the court of first instance has the right to file an appeal within thirty days from the date of service of the judgment or ruling. The appellee, upon receipt of the copy of the appeal petition, shall submit a reply within thirty days. If a party cannot file an appeal or submit a reply within the statutory time limit and applies for an extension, whether to grant the extension shall be decided by the People's Court.

XII. Miscellaneous

114. When the People's Court tries an administrative case, in addition to following the provisions of the Administrative Procedure Law, for matters not covered by these Provisions, reference may be made to the relevant provisions of the Civil Procedure Law.

115. These Provisions shall be implemented on a trial basis from July 11, 1991. All previous judicial interpretations made by the Supreme People's Court that are inconsistent with these Provisions shall be governed by these Provisions.
